body.statement: For a square invertible linear mixture of mutually independent nonconstant sources, of which at most one is Gaussian, the law of the mixture determines the mixing columns, and equivalently the projective rows of the inverse mixing matrix, up to permutation and nonzero coordinatewise scaling.

source.locator: Appendix B.1, Lemma 11, specialized to square invertible mixing matrices
source.verbatim_statement: The model (1) is identifiable, if (i) all source variables are non-normal, or (ii) A is of full column rank and at most one source variable is normal.

upstream.citation: J. Eriksson and V. Koivunen, Identifiability, Separability, and Uniqueness of Linear ICA Models, IEEE Signal Processing Letters 11(7):601–604, 2004, DOI 10.1109/LSP.2004.830118.
upstream.locator: Theorem 3.1; author version in ICA2003 proceedings

attestation.note: Verified in the lawful author-uploaded Eriksson–Koivunen ICA2003 paper, Theorem 3.1. Dai et al. arXiv:2603.04780v1 Appendix B.1 Lemma 11 states the all-non-Gaussian irreducible branch and attributes ICA identifiability to Eriksson–Koivunen; the full-column-rank at-most-one-Gaussian branch used by this square specialization is supplied by the upstream theorem.
